task: P2 install environment (IEC 60664-1 pollution degree + overvoltage category; B14 env_label)

env_label.instructions: Which install environment does the user's description indicate?

criteria.need_more_information: The description does not determine it.

pollution_degree.instructions: Which IEC 60664-1 pollution degree applies to the environment the board's insulation is exposed to?

criteria.pd1: No pollution or only dry, nonconductive pollution occurs. The pollution has no influence.
criteria.pd2: Only nonconductive pollution occurs. However, a temporary conductivity caused by condensation is to be expected.
criteria.pd3: Conductive pollution occurs or dry non-conductive pollution occurs which becomes conductive due to condensation which is to be expected.
criteria.pd4: Continuous conductivity occurs due to conductive dust, rain, or other wet conditions.
criteria.need_more_information: The description does not determine the pollution degree.

overvoltage_category.instructions: Which IEC 60664-1 overvoltage category applies to how the board is powered?

criteria.ovc_i: Circuits connected in a way that takes measures to limit overvoltage transients.
criteria.ovc_ii: Equipment supplied from a fixed installation.
criteria.ovc_iii: Equipment with a fixed installation subject to special requirements.
criteria.ovc_iv: Equipment used at the origin of installation, connected directly to the mains voltage.
criteria.need_more_information: The description does not determine the overvoltage category.

truth_rule: Pollution degree and overvoltage category are set from the IEC 60664-1 definitions as quoted by TI SLLA353A and the examples in TI SLUP419. PD refers to the micro-environment the board sees (sealed/potted/conformal-coated -> PD1). need_more_information when the description omits the deciding fact. env_label (B14 template) truth maps from PD only: pd1->pd1_sealed, pd2->pd2_ovc2_indoor_controlled, pd3->pd3_ovc3_field_wired, pd4->no correct class (excluded from env_label accuracy), NMI->need_more_information.

stricter_option.rule: final = max(Jev argmax, default) per dimension; a need_more_information argmax yields the default. Unsafe error = final below truth on a determinate dimension. Over-design = final above truth.

citations.title: Texas Instruments, Isolation Glossary (SLLA353A, rev. Sep 2017)
citations.quote: Pollution Degree 1 — No pollution or only dry, nonconductive pollution occurs. The pollution has no influence. Pollution Degree 2 — Only nonconductive pollution occurs. However, a temporary conductivity caused by condensation is to be expected. Pollution Degree 3 — Conductive pollution occurs or dry non-conductive pollution occurs which becomes conductive due to condensation which is to be expected. Pollution Degree 4 – Continuous conductivity occurs due to conductive dust, rain, or other wet conditions. ... Overvoltage Categories ... four different levels as indicated in IEC 60664. I: Signal level — Special protected equipment or parts of equipment, for example, circuit board inside a DVD player. II: Local level — Portable equipment that is supplied from the wall outlet ... III: Distribution level — Equipment in fixed installation such as HVAC system ... IV: Primary supply level — Equipment for use at the origin of the installations such as overhead lines, cable systems

citations.title: Texas Instruments, Demystifying Clearance and Creepage Distance for High-Voltage End Equipment (SLUP419, Mar 2024)
citations.quote: Pollution degree 1: ... These systems are sealed to exclude dust and moisture, or the PCB uses conformal coating ... Pollution degree 2: ... labs, offices and enclosures for servers, telecommunications equipment ... Pollution degree 3: ... industrial applications, farming equipment and unheated factory rooms. Pollution degree 4: ... common for outdoor applications. ... Category I: ... circuits connected in a way that takes measures to limit overvoltage transients. Examples include equipment such as 24-VAC thermostats and sprinkler systems connected to the mains through a step-down transformer. Category II: ... equipment supplied from a fixed installation. Examples include equipment plugged into an outlet ... Category III: ... equipment with a fixed installation subject to special requirements. Examples include equipment permanently connected such as switches within a fuse panel, air conditioners or industrial machinery hardwired to the AC mains. Category IV: ... equipment used at the origin of installation ... Examples include electricity meters

state.install_description: The controller sits in a climate-controlled office inside a plastic desktop case. It plugs into a 230 V wall socket and its mains power supply is on the board.

items.derivation: Office, occasional condensation only (PD2, TI SLUP419 'offices'); plugged into an outlet (OVC II, TI SLUP419).

paraphrase_state.install_description: Where it goes: an air-conditioned office, in a plastic box on a desk. Power: a mains cord into a 230 V socket; the power supply is on this board.

state.install_description: A thermostat board on a living-room wall, powered from the furnace's 24 VAC step-down transformer.

items.derivation: Indoor home (PD2); TI SLUP419 names 24-VAC thermostats fed through a step-down transformer as Category I.

state.install_description: The board goes in a ventilated machine cabinet on a metal-stamping shop floor, where metal dust gets in. The cabinet is hardwired to the plant's 400 V three-phase distribution.

items.derivation: Conductive metal dust reaches the board (PD3); industrial machinery hardwired to the mains (OVC III, TI SLUP419).

paraphrase_state.install_description: Location: a metal-stamping plant; the cabinet is ventilated and fine metal dust settles inside. Power: permanently wired to 400 V three-phase distribution.

state.install_description: The board is potted in epoxy inside a hermetically sealed housing and runs from a 3.6 V lithium battery.

items.derivation: Sealed to exclude dust and moisture (PD1, TI SLUP419); no mains connection, battery circuit with no transient source (OVC I).

paraphrase_state.install_description: Epoxy-potted inside a hermetic case; powered by a 3.6 V lithium cell; no mains anywhere.

state.install_description: The board is fixed, with no enclosure, to the outside wall of a cattle shed where rain and snow reach it. It is powered from a 24 VAC Class 2 transformer located indoors.

items.derivation: Rain and snow on the board (PD4); fed through a step-down transformer (OVC I per TI SLUP419's example).

state.install_description: The module mounts inside a sub-distribution board (fuse panel) in a heated office building; its supply is wired directly to the busbar through a breaker.

items.derivation: Heated indoor (PD2); inside a fuse panel, permanently connected (OVC III, TI SLUP419 'switches within a fuse panel').

state.install_description: A plug-in controller (230 V cord and plug) for a workbench in an unheated farm workshop where condensation is expected.

items.derivation: Unheated farm room with expected condensation (PD3, TI SLUP419 'farming equipment and unheated factory rooms'); plugged in (OVC II).

paraphrase_state.install_description: Farm workshop, not heated, condensation expected on cold mornings. The unit has a 230 V plug.

state.install_description: The board is part of a utility electricity meter at the service entrance of a house, in a dry indoor basement, powered from the incoming supply before the main breaker.

items.derivation: Dry indoor (PD2); electricity meter at the origin of the installation (OVC IV, TI SLUP419).

paraphrase_state.install_description: This board lives in the utility's electricity meter where the supply enters the house (dry basement), and it is fed from the incoming line ahead of the main breaker.

state.install_description: The board is sealed in a gasketed IP68 enclosure with a desiccant pack that excludes dust and moisture; the enclosure plugs into a 120 V outlet through a sealed cord.

items.derivation: Sealed to exclude dust and moisture (PD1); plugged into an outlet (OVC II).

state.install_description: A zone controller mounted in the service compartment of a rooftop air-handling unit; the compartment takes in outdoor air and condensation is expected. It is powered from the unit's 24 VAC control transformer.

items.derivation: Condensation expected (PD3); fed through a step-down control transformer (OVC I per TI SLUP419's 24-VAC example).

paraphrase_state.install_description: Installed in a rooftop air handler's service bay that breathes outdoor air, so condensation is expected; supply is the unit's own 24 VAC control transformer.

state.install_description: A benchtop instrument board for a university electronics lab, supplied through a detachable IEC mains cord.
